key_insight: HGTO reframes topology optimization as a unified graph-based, physics-informed problem that couples element densities and structural equilibrium directly on the finite-element mesh.
engineering_relevance: This makes topology optimization more mesh-aware and computationally efficient while supporting irregular meshes, 3D problems, finite deformation, and elastoplasticity.
method: Element densities are parameterized on the element graph derived from the mesh.
Structural state is solved on a node-element hypergraph with explicit finite-element kinematics, quadrature, constitutive response, and force assembly.
The material field and equilibrium state are coupled through the same finite-element incidence structure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports compliance comparable to conventional density-based optimization, with substantially lower computational cost than a representative coordinate-based dual-field neural method.
watch_item: Performance still depends on correct graph/hypergraph construction and differentiable finite-element implementation, which may be complex for large or highly nonlinear models.
paper_title: HGTO: A Unified Graph-Based Physics-Informed Formulation for Structural Topology Optimization
